title: Constellations
seo_title: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: Constellations Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: Stars form patterns called constellations, which appear to move across the sky because of the Earth's rotation and change with the seasons because of the Earth's revolution. Farmers and travellers have long used stars to mark planting time and find directions. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 6, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): constellations, why stars seem to move, stars and their colours, galaxies and the night sky. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A constellation is a pattern of stars.
key_sub: Stars seem to move because the Earth rotates.
body_html:
How to think about it

A constellation is a group of stars that forms a pattern, such as Orion, the Southern Cross (Crux) and Scorpius. Stars seem to rise in the east and set in the west because the Earth rotates; we see different constellations in different months because the Earth revolves around the Sun.

Stars are huge balls of hot gas; their colours show their temperature. Our Sun is one star among billions in the Milky Way galaxy. Long ago, farmers in many parts of Africa watched certain stars, such as the Pleiades, to know when the planting season was near.

Example

Which constellation has three stars in a row as a belt?

A hunter

Answer: Orion

Example

Why do stars seem to move at night?

The Earth spins.

Answer: the Earth rotates

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the stars in a constellation are close together in space.
  • Thinking stars only come out at night (they are there in the day too).
  • Thinking all stars are the same colour.

faq.q: Why can we see more stars in the province than in the city?

faq.a: They used the positions of stars to find directions at night.

items.q: Light from the sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. Light from Proxima Centauri takes 4.2 years. Why does the sun look so much brighter?
c: Proxima Centauri is a planet, not a star.
The sun is the biggest star in the universe.
The sun is much, much closer to Earth.
The sun is the only star that gives off light.
items.e: The sun is about 8 light-minutes away; Proxima Centauri is 4.2 light-years away. Distance makes the difference.

items.q: In the life of a Sun-like star, what stage comes just before the planetary nebula stage?

items.q: Evidence: Almost every distant galaxy's light is redshifted. What does it support?
c: We see them as they were billions of years ago, when the universe was younger.
Space itself is stretching everywhere (Hubble's law).
This matches what the Big Bang model predicts for the first few minutes.
items.e: Three main lines of evidence: redshift, the CMB and light-element abundances.

items.e: Match the evidence to the idea.
